# Independent audit: four and five positive interval fibers

The following proofs pass without a mathematical correction:

- `candidate b9d705e0e5ad374f`;
- `candidate d67c525eee8e41c8`.

The conclusions have their stated finite scope. In both files every
nonempty integer fiber is assumed to have positive length and the
actual mixed centroid is assumed to have integer base. Neither audit
removes those hypotheses or infers an arbitrary-fiber theorem.

## Common normalization and cap accounting

Convexity makes the integer indices consecutive and the lower endpoint
sequence convex and upper endpoint sequence concave. Their difference
is a positive concave width sequence. An integer base translation,
continuous translation, and invertible affine continuous shear turn an
arbitrary nonvertical cap through the true centroid into `x>=0` while
preserving the lattice, centroid equations, and length ratios.

For both normalized families, the continuous centroid equation is

    sum w_i r_i=Q/2,  Q=sum w_i^2.

Jensen with the positive probability weights `w_i/M` and base mean
zero proves

    r_0>=Q/(2M)>0,   l_0<=-Q/(2M)<0.

Thus the central fiber is properly cut; its contribution is `r_0`.
Whenever a noncentral fiber is not wholly captured, its contribution is
exactly `(r_i)_+`, even if the whole fiber is excluded or only its right
endpoint belongs to the cap. A wholly captured fiber is characterized
by `l_i>=0`, including equality. These conventions are used consistently
in every displayed cap formula.

## Four fibers

Positivity excludes either extreme index as the integer mean. Reflection
and translation therefore reduce the mean to zero on `-1,0,1,2`.
Normalizing `w_1=1` and using the integer moment gives widths

    (1+2t,s,1,t).

The two width-concavity inequalities are precisely
`s>=1+t` and `s<=2-t`, hence `0<t<=1/2`. The maximum width is
`max(s,1+2t)`. The derivative checks in the two branches of
`4Q>=3 w_max M` are valid throughout this region: the first derivative
is `2s-6-9t<0`, and the second is `8s-3-6t>=5+2t>0`.
The endpoint values are exactly `30t^2` and `3-6t`.

If no fiber is captured wholly, dropping only negative upper endpoints
gives `w_max F>=Q/2`, proving the asserted `3/8` bound.
If the leftmost fiber is captured, its length is at least `M/4`.
If fiber 1 is captured, convexity of the lower endpoints and `l_0<0`
force fiber 2 to be captured too, and their combined length is at least
`M/4`. In both cases this captured mass is disjoint from the central
contribution, and `r_0>=Q/(2M)>=M/8` follows from four-term Cauchy.
This covers every captured subset except the singleton `{2}`.

For that singleton, `r_2>=t` and `r_2<=2r_1-r_0` imply `r_1>0`.
Eliminating `r_2` from the moment identity yields the coefficients

    (1+2t)[(r_-1)_+ +r_1]+(s-t)r_0.

All three cap variables here are nonnegative. Taking their maximum
coefficient proves `F>=Q/(2K)+t`, with `K=max(1+2t,s-t)`.
The two remaining polynomial bounds are correct. In the first branch,
the derivative in `s` is at least `5+2t`, and the value at `s=1+t`
is `3+2t+16t^2`. In the second branch the expression

    (s-2)(s-4)+2st+22t+21t^2

is positive because `1<s<2` and `t>0`.

The two vertical cap masses are exactly `s+1+t` and `1+2t+s`, both
strictly above `M/2`; the central boundary fiber is included.

The finite-family auxiliary inequality in Section 7 is also valid:
for `N>1`, Cauchy on the nonmaximal weights and the arithmetic-geometric
mean inequality give

    Q/(HM)>=[N(H/M)-2+M/H]/(N-1)
             >=2/(1+sqrt(N)).

For `N=1` the centered interval has half its length in the cap.

## Five fibers

The excluded off-center integer means are handled completely. If the
mean were the second index, normalizing the next width to one gives
`(1+2t+3u,s,1,t,u)` on `-1,0,1,2,3`. Concavity forces both
`t<=1/2-3u/4` and `t>=(1+u)/2`, impossible for `u>0`.
Reflection handles the other off-center interior index; positivity
excludes the extreme indices. The middle index is therefore the only
possible integer mean.

The normalization of its equal first moments on either side gives

    (a,1-2a,c,1-2b,b).

The three width-concavity inequalities are exactly
`c>=1-a-b`, `c<=2-5a`, `c<=2-5b`. They imply `a,b<=1/3`
by comparing the larger of `a,b` with the two inequalities
`4a-b<=1`, `4b-a<=1`. Together with `a,b>0` the resulting parameter
space describes positive widths and includes all feasible cases.

The no-captured-fiber case has cap fraction at least
`1/(1+sqrt(5))>1/4`. A captured inner neighbor forces the adjacent
outer fiber to be captured. The combined block already exceeds `M/4`:
the right and left excesses are bounded below by `a+2b` and `2a+b`
after multiplying by four. Thus only the captured subsets `{2}`,
`{-2}`, and `{-2,2}` remain.

For the right singleton, eliminating the right outer upper endpoint
gives

    Q/2 <= a(r_-2)_+ +(1-2a)(r_-1)_+
              +(c-b)r_0+r_1.

The coefficients of the first, second, and last terms are at most
one; every variable is nonnegative. This proves the bound with
`K=max(1,c-b)`. The polynomial expansions in both branches are exact.
For `K=1`, replacing `c` by `1-a-b` is valid because
`4c-1>=1/3`. The resulting quadratic decreases in `a` throughout the
full square `[0,1/3]^2`: its derivative is at most `-2/3`.
Its value at `a=1/3` is

    12(b-7/36)^2+59/108>0.

Using the full square for this lower bound is legitimate even if the
endpoint chosen is outside the smaller feasible parameter region.
For `K=c-b>=1`, the derivative in `c` is at least `a+8b>0`.
At `c=1+b` the expression is `3-7a+10a^2+12b^2`, bounded below
by `16/9` because `-7+20a<0` on `[0,1/3]`.

When both outer fibers are captured, eliminating both outer upper
endpoints gives exactly

    Q/2<=r_-1+r_1+(c-a-b)r_0.

All three middle upper endpoints are positive. With `A=a+b` and
`B=a^2+b^2`, the branch `K=1` is bounded below by

    3-6A+2A^2+10B
      >=3-6A+7A^2
       =7(A-3/7)^2+12/7.

For `K=c-A>=1`, the derivative in `c` is at least `8A>0`;
substitution of `c=1+A` gives exactly `3+2A^2+10B>0`.
This exhausts the sign patterns.

The two vertical cap masses `1-a+c` and `1-b+c` exceed `M/2`
because `c-|a-b|>=1-2max(a,b)>=1/3`. Both contain the entire
central boundary fiber. Finally each actual centroid belongs to the
compact convex body and has integer base, hence belongs to its
mixed-integer intersection. Moving any containing closed halfspace
parallel to the centroid only decreases its mass.

## Exact arithmetic check

In addition to the inequality arguments above, independent symbolic
expansion verified all 17 quadratic identities and endpoint
substitutions appearing in the two case analyses. The proof does not
depend on numerical optimization or a finite sample of parameter
values. No unresolved sign pattern, boundary convention, or constant
loss remains.
